clinician.trajectory_summary: A young man in his 20s with pre-existing atopic dermatitis and lumbar disk hernia presented with a 4-day history of chills, fever (38.7°C), headache, vomiting, and back pain, along with a painless rash on the right occipital region. Initial outpatient treatment with cefditoren pivoxil was ineffective. He was referred to hospital for further evaluation. Lumbar puncture on admission revealed clear, colorless CSF with lymphocytic predominance on Gram stain, no bacteria detected, and low glucose (28 mg/dL). Bacterial and mycobacterial cultures from CSF and blood cultures were negative. HSV PCR was negative. VZV PCR from CSF confirmed VZV DNA at 11×10^6 copies/mL, establishing the diagnosis of VZV meningitis. A dermatologist evaluated the worsening occipital rash during hospitalization and diagnosed herpes zoster based on rash characteristics and associated pain. Intravenous acyclovir (10 mg/kg every 8 hours) and ampicillin (2 g every 6 hours) were initiated; ampicillin was discontinued after negative cultures. MRI revealed no abnormal intracranial signals. After 5 days of intravenous acyclovir treatment, the patient's fever resolved and symptoms improved. He was discharged with 5 days of oral valacyclovir 1000 mg three times per day.
